title: Genesis 8 — The waters recede, the altar built

paragraphs.text: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֙וּחַ֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃

i18n.en: The Elohim remembered Noah, and every wild animal and every domesticated animal that was with him in the ark; and the Elohim caused a breath to pass over the land, and the waters subsided.
i18n.he: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֙וּחַ֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃
i18n.de: Die Elohim gedachten Noahs und jedes Wildtieres und jedes Haustieres, das mit ihm in der Arche war; und die Elohim ließen einen Odem über das Land fahren, und die Wasser sanken.
i18n.es: Los Elohim se acordaron de Noé, y de todo animal salvaje y de todo animal doméstico que estaba con él en el arca; y los Elohim hicieron pasar un aliento sobre la tierra, y las aguas decrecieron.
i18n.fr: Les Elohim se souvinrent de Noé, et de toute bête sauvage et de tout animal domestique qui étaient avec lui dans l'arche ; et les Elohim firent passer un souffle sur la terre, et les eaux s'apaisèrent.
i18n.ja: エロヒムはノアを覚えられた——また彼と共に箱舟にいたすべての野の獣とすべての家畜とを。そしてエロヒムは地の上に息を吹き渡らせ、水は引いていった。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 노아를, 그리고 그와 함께 방주에 있던 모든 들짐승과 모든 가축을 기억하셨다; 엘로힘이 땅 위에 숨을 지나가게 하시니, 물이 잦아들었다.
i18n.ru: И вспомнили Элохим о Ное и о всяком диком звере и о всяком домашнем скоте, что был с ним в ковчеге; и навели Элохим дыхание на землю, и утихли воды.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音记念挪亚和一切与他同在方舟里的野兽与家畜；厄罗音使一股气息掠过大地，水势就消退了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音記念挪亞，以及與他同在方舟裡的一切野獸和家畜；厄羅音使一股氣息掠過大地，諸水就消退了。

paragraphs.commentary:
**Two echoes of Genesis 1 in a single verse.**

First, *vayyizkor* — *the Elohim remembered*. After 150 days of prevailing waters at the close of chapter 7, with no divine action recorded across that stretch, the chapter opens with a turning verb. The same verb will mark each major covenantal turning point in the Hebrew Bible: 'YHWH remembered Sarah' (Gen 21:1), 'the Elohim remembered Rachel' (30:22), 'the Elohim remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob' at the start of the Exodus (Ex 2:24). In every case, *remembering* names the moment when divine attention returns to the preserved-and-waiting individual after a long stretch. The chapter is doing a literary thing it will do again at every covenantal hinge.

Second, *vayya'aver Elohim ruach al ha-aretz* — *the Elohim caused a breath to pass over the land*. Compare Gen 1:2: *ruach Elohim merachefet al p'nei ha-mayim* — *the breath of the Elohim was hovering over the face of the waters*. Same noun (*ruach*), same agents, the same waters being acted on. The chapter is rebooting Genesis 1's grammar. The un-creation of the Flood is being reversed into a *re-creation*, with the same divine *ruach* serving as the medium. What hovered over the waters at the beginning now passes over the land at the resumption.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסָּֽכְרוּ֙ מַעְיְנֹ֣ת תְּה֔וֹם וַֽאֲרֻבֹּ֖ת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיִּכָּלֵ֥א הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם מִן־הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: The fountains of the deep and the floodgates of the skies were closed, and the rain from the skies was held back.
i18n.he: וַיִּסָּֽכְרוּ֙ מַעְיְנֹ֣ת תְּה֔וֹם וַֽאֲרֻבֹּ֖ת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיִּכָּלֵ֥א הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם מִן־הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
i18n.de: Die Quellen der Tiefe und die Schleusen der Himmel wurden verschlossen, und der Regen vom Himmel wurde zurückgehalten.
i18n.es: Las fuentes del abismo y las compuertas de los cielos fueron cerradas, y la lluvia de los cielos fue retenida.
i18n.fr: Les sources de l'abîme et les écluses des cieux se fermèrent, et la pluie des cieux fut retenue.
i18n.ja: 深淵の源と天の窓は閉じられ、天からの雨は止められた。
i18n.ko: 깊음의 샘들과 하늘의 창들이 닫혔고, 하늘로부터의 비가 멈추었다.
i18n.ru: И закрылись источники бездны и окна небес, и удержан был дождь с небес.
i18n.zh: 深渊的源头与诸天的窗户都关闭了，诸天的雨也止住了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 深淵的源頭和諸天的窗戶都關閉了，從諸天而來的雨也止住了。

paragraphs.commentary: **The reversal reversed.** The two cosmic openings of 7:11 — the *fountains of the great deep* and the *floodgates of the skies* — are now *closed*. The verbs are passive (niphal): *vayyissakhru* ('were closed', from סָכַר sakar — to shut, stop up) and *vayyikkale* ('was held back', from כָּלָא kala — to restrain, withhold). The chapter is undoing 7:11 with mirror-grammar. The raqia of Genesis 1, breached in 7:11, is now resealed; the lower waters of Genesis 1, released in 7:11, are now contained. The cosmological collapse of chapter 7 is structurally reversed in two verbs of chapter 8.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ הַמַּ֛יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָ֖רֶץ הָל֣וֹךְ וָשׁ֑וֹב וַיַּחְסְר֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם מִקְצֵ֕ה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: The waters receded from upon the land, going and returning; and at the end of one hundred and fifty days the waters had diminished.
i18n.he: וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ הַמַּ֛יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָ֖רֶץ הָל֣וֹךְ וָשׁ֑וֹב וַיַּחְסְר֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם מִקְצֵ֕ה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃
i18n.de: Und die Wasser wichen vom Land, gehend und kehrend; und am Ende von hundertfünfzig Tagen hatten die Wasser abgenommen.
i18n.es: Las aguas se retiraron de sobre la tierra, yendo y regresando; y al cabo de ciento cincuenta días las aguas habían disminuido.
i18n.fr: Les eaux se retirèrent de dessus la terre, allant et revenant ; et au bout de cent cinquante jours les eaux avaient diminué.
i18n.ja: 水は地の上から、行きまた戻りつつ退いていった。百五十日の終わりに、水は減っていた。
i18n.ko: 물이 땅에서 점점 물러갔으니, 가고 또 돌아갔다; 백오십 일이 지난 후에 물이 줄어들었다.
i18n.ru: И стали воды отступать с земли, отходя и возвращаясь; и к концу ста пятидесяти дней убыли воды.
i18n.zh: 水从大地上渐渐退去，去而复来；过了一百五十天，水势就减退了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 諸水從大地上漸漸退去，去而復返；過了一百五十日，諸水減少了。

paragraphs.text: וַתָּ֤נַח הַתֵּבָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָה־עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט׃

i18n.en: In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
i18n.he: וַתָּ֤נַח הַתֵּבָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָה־עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט׃
i18n.de: Und im siebten Monat, am siebzehnten Tag des Monats, ruhte die Arche auf den Bergen Ararat.
i18n.es: En el séptimo mes, en el día diecisiete del mes, el arca se posó sobre los montes de Ararat.
i18n.fr: Le septième mois, le dix-septième jour du mois, l'arche s'arrêta sur les montagnes d'Ararat.
i18n.ja: 第七の月、その月の十七日に、箱舟はアララト山の上にとどまった。
i18n.ko: 일곱째 달 그 달 십칠일에, 방주가 아라랏 산들 위에 머물렀다.
i18n.ru: И остановился ковчег в седьмом месяце, в семнадцатый день месяца, на горах Арарат.
i18n.zh: 七月十七日，方舟停在亚拉腊山上。
i18n.zh-Hant: 七月十七日，方舟停在亞拉臘山上。

paragraphs.commentary:
**The ark *rests*.** The verb תָּנַח tanach is from נוּחַ nuach — the same root as *Noah's* name (5:29). The ark of Noah comes-to-rest on the mountains of Ararat. The chapter's name-and-verb wordplay is structural: the *resting one* (Noach) is in a *resting* (tanach) vessel; the rest happens exactly when the divine *ruach* has done its work over the waters.

The date — seventh month, seventeenth day — is precisely five months (150 days) after the Flood began (7:11: second month, seventeenth day). The chapter is keeping a calendar; the durations are not symbolic durations only but counted days. The five months equal 150 days only if each month is exactly 30 days — implying the chapter uses a schematic 30-day-month, 360-day-year calendar (the same calendar later used in 1 Enoch's astronomical book and in priestly liturgical reckoning). The chapter's calendrical care is precise enough to surface its own calendrical assumptions.

*Harei Ararat* — **mountains** of Ararat, plural. The Hebrew specifies a mountainous *region* (Urartu, around Lake Van in eastern Anatolia / Armenia), not a single peak. The traditional identification of *Mount* Ararat (Ağrı Dağı in Turkey, 5,137m) became fixed in late antique and medieval Christian tradition; the Hebrew is broader.

paragraphs.text: וְהַמַּ֗יִם הָיוּ֙ הָל֣וֹךְ וְחָס֔וֹר עַ֖ד הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽעֲשִׂירִ֑י בָּֽעֲשִׂירִי֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ נִרְא֖וּ רָאשֵׁ֥י הֶֽהָרִֽים׃

i18n.en: The waters continued to recede until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
i18n.he: וְהַמַּ֗יִם הָיוּ֙ הָל֣וֹךְ וְחָס֔וֹר עַ֖ד הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽעֲשִׂירִ֑י בָּֽעֲשִׂירִי֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ נִרְא֖וּ רָאשֵׁ֥י הֶֽהָרִֽים׃
i18n.de: Und die Wasser nahmen weiterhin ab bis zum zehnten Monat; im zehnten Monat, am ersten Tag des Monats, erschienen die Gipfel der Berge.
i18n.es: Las aguas siguieron decreciendo hasta el décimo mes; en el décimo mes, en el primer día del mes, aparecieron las cumbres de los montes.
i18n.fr: Les eaux continuèrent de décroître jusqu'au dixième mois ; le dixième mois, le premier jour du mois, les sommets des montagnes apparurent.
i18n.ja: 水は第十の月まで減り続け、第十の月、その月の一日に、山々の頂が現れた。
i18n.ko: 물은 열째 달까지 계속 물러갔다; 열째 달 그 달 초하루에 산들의 봉우리들이 나타났다.
i18n.ru: А воды продолжали убывать до десятого месяца; в десятом месяце, в первый день месяца, показались вершины гор.
i18n.zh: 水继续减退，直到十月；十月初一日，群山的顶就显露出来了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 諸水繼續消退，直到十月；十月初一日，諸山的頂顯露出來。

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֑וֹם וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח נֹ֔חַ אֶת־חַלּ֥וֹן הַתֵּבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

i18n.en: At the end of forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made.
i18n.he: וַֽיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֑וֹם וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח נֹ֔חַ אֶת־חַלּ֥וֹן הַתֵּבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
i18n.de: Und es geschah am Ende von vierzig Tagen, daß Noah das Fenster der Arche öffnete, das er gemacht hatte.
i18n.es: Al cabo de cuarenta días, Noé abrió la ventana del arca que había hecho.
i18n.fr: Au bout de quarante jours, Noé ouvrit la fenêtre de l'arche qu'il avait faite.
i18n.ja: 四十日の終わりに、ノアは自らが造った箱舟の窓を開いた。
i18n.ko: 사십 일이 지난 후에 노아가 자기가 만든 방주의 창을 열었다.
i18n.ru: И по прошествии сорока дней открыл Ной окно ковчега, которое сделал.
i18n.zh: 过了四十天，挪亚打开他所造的方舟的窗户。
i18n.zh-Hant: 過了四十日，挪亞打開他所造的方舟的窗戶，

paragraphs.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־הָֽעֹרֵ֑ב וַיֵּצֵ֤א יָצוֹא֙ וָשׁ֔וֹב עַד־יְבֹ֥שֶׁת הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: He sent out the raven, and it went out, going to and fro, until the waters dried up from the land.
i18n.he: וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־הָֽעֹרֵ֑ב וַיֵּצֵ֤א יָצוֹא֙ וָשׁ֔וֹב עַד־יְבֹ֥שֶׁת הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Und er ließ den Raben aus, und er flog aus, hin und her, bis die Wasser vom Land vertrocknet waren.
i18n.es: Envió al cuervo, y este salió, yendo y volviendo, hasta que las aguas se secaron de sobre la tierra.
i18n.fr: Il lâcha le corbeau, qui sortit, allant et venant, jusqu'à ce que les eaux fussent séchées de dessus la terre.
i18n.ja: 彼はからすを放った。それは出て行き、水が地から乾くまで、行きつ戻りつしていた。
i18n.ko: 그는 까마귀를 내보냈고, 그것은 물이 땅에서 마를 때까지 이리저리 오가며 나갔다.
i18n.ru: И выпустил ворона, и тот вылетал и возвращался, пока не высохли воды на земле.
i18n.zh: 他放出乌鸦去；乌鸦飞来飞去，直到水从大地上干了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他放出一隻烏鴉，烏鴉便飛來飛去，直到諸水從大地上乾涸。

paragraphs.commentary:
**The raven first.** Noah sends out *ha-orev* — the raven — and it leaves and returns repeatedly without reporting back conclusively. The Mesopotamian flood narratives (Gilgamesh Tablet XI, Atrahasis) have a different bird-sequence: Utnapishtim sends a dove, then a swallow, then a raven — and the raven *does not return*, signaling the waters have receded. Genesis has reversed the order: raven first, dove second, and the *dove*'s behavior is what tells Noah the land has dried.

The raven's *going to and fro* (יָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב yatzo va-shov, an infinitive-absolute construction) is iterative — the bird shuttles without settling. The raven is *unclean* (by later Levitical categorization, Lev 11:15) and a carrion-eater; the chapter's logic is that the raven could subsist on floating bodies and emerging carcasses, requiring no settled landing. The dove, by contrast, will return because there is *nowhere clean* yet to alight. The two birds' contrasting behaviors are not arbitrary — they reflect each species' ecological capacity.

paragraphs.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מֵאִתּ֑וֹ לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲקַ֣לּוּ הַמַּ֔יִם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then he sent out the dove from him, to see whether the waters had lightened from the face of the ground.
i18n.he: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מֵאִתּ֑וֹ לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲקַ֣לּוּ הַמַּ֔יִם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
i18n.de: Dann ließ er die Taube von sich aus, um zu sehen, ob die Wasser sich vom Angesicht des Ackerbodens verringert hätten.
i18n.es: Entonces envió a la paloma desde él, para ver si las aguas habían menguado de la faz del suelo.
i18n.fr: Puis il lâcha la colombe d'auprès de lui, pour voir si les eaux avaient diminué de la face du sol.
i18n.ja: 次に彼は鳩を自分のもとから放った——大地の面から水が引いたかどうかを見るためである。
i18n.ko: 그런 후 그는 비둘기를 자기에게서 내보내, 물이 경작할 땅의 표면에서 가벼워졌는지 알아보았다.
i18n.ru: Потом выпустил от себя голубя, чтобы видеть, сошла ли вода с лица земли.
i18n.zh: 他又从自己那里放出鸽子去，要看水是否从土地之面减退了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他又從那裡放出一隻鴿子，要看看諸水是否從土壤的表面減退了。

paragraphs.text: וְלֹֽא־מָצְאָה֩ הַיּוֹנָ֨ה מָנ֜וֹחַ לְכַף־רַגְלָ֗הּ וַתָּ֤שָׁב אֵלָיו֙ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֔ה כִּי־מַ֖יִם עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיִּקָּחֶ֔הָ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛הּ אֵלָ֖יו אֶל־הַתֵּבָֽה׃

i18n.en: But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him to the ark, for the waters were on the face of all the land. He put out his hand and took her, and brought her to him into the ark.
i18n.he: וְלֹֽא־מָצְאָה֩ הַיּוֹנָ֨ה מָנ֜וֹחַ לְכַף־רַגְלָ֗הּ וַתָּ֤שָׁב אֵלָיו֙ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֔ה כִּי־מַ֖יִם עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיִּקָּחֶ֔הָ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛הּ אֵלָ֖יו אֶל־הַתֵּבָֽה׃
i18n.de: Aber die Taube fand keinen Ruheplatz für ihre Fußsohle und kehrte zu ihm in die Arche zurück, denn die Wasser waren auf dem Angesicht des ganzen Landes. Da streckte er seine Hand aus und nahm sie und brachte sie zu sich in die Arche.
i18n.es: Pero la paloma no halló lugar de reposo para la planta de su pie, y volvió a él al arca, pues las aguas estaban sobre la faz de toda la tierra. Él extendió su mano y la tomó, y la metió consigo al arca.
i18n.fr: Mais la colombe ne trouva pas de lieu où poser la plante de son pied, et elle revint à lui dans l'arche, car les eaux étaient sur la face de toute la terre. Il tendit la main et la prit, et la fit rentrer auprès de lui dans l'arche.
i18n.ja: しかし鳩は、その足の裏を休める場所を見いださず、彼のもとに、箱舟へ戻ってきた。水がなお全地の面にあったからである。彼は手を伸ばして鳩を取り、彼のもとに、箱舟の中へ取り入れた。
i18n.ko: 그러나 비둘기는 자기 발바닥을 디딜 안식처를 찾지 못하여, 그에게 방주로 돌아왔으니, 물이 온 땅의 표면 위에 있었기 때문이다. 그가 손을 내밀어 그것을 잡고 자기에게로, 방주 안으로 들여놓았다.
i18n.ru: Но не нашёл голубь места покоя для ноги своей и возвратился к нему в ковчег, ибо вода была на лице всей земли. И простёр он руку свою, и взял его, и внёс его к себе в ковчег.
i18n.zh: 但鸽子找不到落脚之处，就回到方舟挪亚那里，因为水还在全地之面上。他伸手把鸽子接进方舟里。
i18n.zh-Hant: 但鴿子找不到落腳之處，便回到方舟裡他那裡，因為諸水仍在全地的表面。他便伸手把牠接進方舟。

paragraphs.commentary: **The resting-place vocabulary.** *Manoach l-khaf-raglah* — *a resting-place for the sole of her foot*. The noun מָנוֹחַ manoach is again from the root נוּחַ nuach — *rest, settle*. The chapter's *Noah* / *Noach* / *tanach* / *manoach* wordplay continues: the *resting one* (Noach) sends the dove to look for a *resting-place* (*manoach*), and the dove cannot find one — yet. Noah gently *takes her* (וַיִּקָּחֶהָ vayyiqqachehah) — the verbal tenderness is striking after the chapter's mass-extinction vocabulary; *put out his hand* (*vayyishlach yado*) and *brought her in*. The interaction is small-scale, intimate, and named in domestic verbs.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֛סֶף שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מִן־הַתֵּבָֽה׃

i18n.en: He waited another seven days, and again sent the dove out from the ark.
i18n.he: וַיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֛סֶף שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מִן־הַתֵּבָֽה׃
i18n.de: Und er wartete noch weitere sieben Tage und ließ die Taube wieder aus der Arche aus.
i18n.es: Esperó otros siete días, y volvió a enviar la paloma desde el arca.
i18n.fr: Il attendit encore sept autres jours, et de nouveau il lâcha la colombe hors de l'arche.
i18n.ja: 彼はさらに七日待ち、再び鳩を箱舟から放った。
i18n.ko: 그는 다시 이레를 기다리고, 또다시 방주에서 비둘기를 내보냈다.
i18n.ru: И помедлил ещё семь дней, и снова выпустил голубя из ковчега.
i18n.zh: 他又等了七天，再从方舟把鸽子放出去。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他又等了七日，再從方舟把鴿子放出去。

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֨א אֵלָ֤יו הַיּוֹנָה֙ לְעֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב וְהִנֵּ֥ה עֲלֵה־זַ֖יִת טָרָ֣ף בְּפִ֑יהָ וַיֵּ֣דַע נֹ֔חַ כִּי־קַ֥לּוּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: The dove came to him at evening time — and behold, a fresh olive leaf in her mouth! Noah knew that the waters had lightened from upon the land.
i18n.he: וַתָּבֹ֨א אֵלָ֤יו הַיּוֹנָה֙ לְעֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב וְהִנֵּ֥ה עֲלֵה־זַ֖יִת טָרָ֣ף בְּפִ֑יהָ וַיֵּ֣דַע נֹ֔חַ כִּי־קַ֥לּוּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Und die Taube kam zu ihm zur Abendzeit — und siehe, ein frisches Olivenblatt in ihrem Schnabel! Da erkannte Noah, daß die Wasser sich vom Land verringert hatten.
i18n.es: La paloma vino a él al atardecer—y he aquí, una hoja fresca de olivo en su pico. Noé supo entonces que las aguas habían menguado de sobre la tierra.
i18n.fr: La colombe revint à lui sur le soir — et voici, une feuille d'olivier fraîche dans son bec ! Noé connut alors que les eaux avaient diminué de dessus la terre.
i18n.ja: 鳩は夕暮れ時に彼のもとに来た——見よ、新しいオリーブの葉をその口にくわえていた。ノアは、水が地から引いたことを知った。
i18n.ko: 비둘기는 저녁때에 그에게로 왔으니 — 보라, 그 입에 갓 딴 올리브 잎이 있었다! 노아는 물이 땅 위에서 가벼워졌음을 알았다.
i18n.ru: И пришёл к нему голубь в вечернее время — и вот, свежий масличный лист в клюве его! И узнал Ной, что сошла вода с земли.
i18n.zh: 到了晚上，鸽子回到他那里——看哪，嘴里有一片新鲜的橄榄叶！挪亚就知道水从大地上减退了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 到了晚上，鴿子回到他那裡—看哪，嘴裡銜著一片新摘的橄欖葉！挪亞就知道諸水已從大地上減退了。

paragraphs.commentary:
**The chapter's iconic image.** Two verbal precisions and a botanical note.

The verb טָרַף taraf has two senses: *plucked* (active — the dove plucked it) or *fresh* / *newly-broken-off* (stative passive — the leaf was new). Modern translations favor *fresh*: the leaf is new growth, evidence that vegetation has *resumed* on the land. The chapter's evidence is botanical: there is now a re-emerging biosphere.

The choice of olive is precise. The olive tree (Olea europaea) is one of the most flood-resistant and quickly-regenerating Mediterranean species, capable of resprouting from roots after extended submersion. ANE-Mediterranean farmers knew this; the olive was the tree one would *expect* to see leafing first. The chapter's botany is observational, not arbitrary.

The image — *yonah carrying a fresh olive leaf* — will become one of the Hebrew Bible's most-reproduced icons. Christian art will make the dove the Holy Spirit; modern peace iconography will use the olive branch as its sign. The chapter does neither — it simply records evening, dove, olive, knowledge. The afterlife of the image dwarfs its modest verse.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיְשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־הַיּוֹנָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יָסְפָ֥ה שׁוּב־אֵלָ֖יו עֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: He waited another seven days, and sent out the dove; and she did not return to him again.
i18n.he: וַיִּיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיְשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־הַיּוֹנָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יָסְפָ֥ה שׁוּב־אֵלָ֖יו עֽוֹד׃
i18n.de: Und er wartete noch weitere sieben Tage und ließ die Taube aus; und sie kehrte nicht wieder zu ihm zurück.
i18n.es: Esperó otros siete días, y envió a la paloma; y ella no volvió más a él.
i18n.fr: Il attendit encore sept autres jours, et lâcha la colombe ; et elle ne revint plus à lui.
i18n.ja: 彼はさらに七日待って、鳩を放った。すると鳩はもはや彼のもとに戻らなかった。
i18n.ko: 그는 다시 이레를 기다리고 비둘기를 내보냈는데; 그녀는 그에게로 다시 돌아오지 않았다.
i18n.ru: И помедлил ещё семь дней, и выпустил голубя; и не возвратился он к нему более.
i18n.zh: 他又等了七天，把鸽子放出去；鸽子就不再回到他那里了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他又等了七日，再放出鴿子；鴿子就不再回到他那裡了。

paragraphs.text: וַֽ֠יְהִי בְּאַחַ֨ת וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֜וֹת שָׁנָ֗ה בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חָֽרְב֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּ֤סַר נֹ֙חַ֙ אֶת־מִכְסֵ֣ה הַתֵּבָ֔ה וַיַּ֕רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה חָֽרְב֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: In the six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters dried up from on the land. Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked — and behold, the face of the ground had dried.
i18n.he: וַֽ֠יְהִי בְּאַחַ֨ת וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֜וֹת שָׁנָ֗ה בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חָֽרְב֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּ֤סַר נֹ֙חַ֙ אֶת־מִכְסֵ֣ה הַתֵּבָ֔ה וַיַּ֕רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה חָֽרְב֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
i18n.de: Und es geschah im sechshundertundersten Jahr, am ersten Tag des ersten Monats, daß die Wasser vom Land vertrocknet waren. Da entfernte Noah die Decke der Arche und schaute — und siehe, das Angesicht des Ackerbodens war vertrocknet.
i18n.es: En el año seiscientos uno, en el primer día del primer mes, las aguas se secaron de sobre la tierra. Noé quitó la cubierta del arca y miró—y he aquí, la faz del suelo se había secado.
i18n.fr: L'an six cent un, le premier jour du premier mois, les eaux avaient séché de dessus la terre. Noé ôta la couverture de l'arche et regarda — et voici, la face du sol avait séché.
i18n.ja: 第六百一年、第一の月、その月の一日に、水は地から乾いた。ノアは箱舟の覆いを取り除いて見た——見よ、大地の面は乾いていた。
i18n.ko: 육백한 살이 되던 해, 첫째 달 초하루에, 물이 땅에서 말랐다. 노아가 방주의 덮개를 벗기고 보니 — 보라, 경작할 땅의 표면이 말라 있었다.
i18n.ru: В шестьсот первом году, в первый день первого месяца, иссякла вода с земли. И снял Ной кровлю ковчега и посмотрел — и вот, обсохло лицо земли.
i18n.zh: 六百零一年正月初一日，水从大地上干了。挪亚揭开方舟的盖观看——看哪，土地之面已经干了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 到了六百零一年，正月初一日，諸水從大地上乾涸了。挪亞揭開方舟的蓋子觀看—看哪，土壤的表面已經乾了。

paragraphs.text: וּבַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ יָבְשָׁ֖ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the land was dry.
i18n.he: וּבַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ יָבְשָׁ֖ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃ (ס)
i18n.de: Und im zweiten Monat, am siebenundzwanzigsten Tag des Monats, war das Land trocken.
i18n.es: En el segundo mes, en el día veintisiete del mes, la tierra estaba seca.
i18n.fr: Le deuxième mois, le vingt-septième jour du mois, la terre fut sèche.
i18n.ja: 第二の月、その月の二十七日に、地は乾いた。
i18n.ko: 둘째 달, 그 달 이십칠일에, 땅이 말랐다.
i18n.ru: А во втором месяце, в двадцать седьмой день месяца, высохла земля.
i18n.zh: 二月二十七日，大地就干了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 到了二月二十七日，大地都乾了。

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־נֹ֥חַ לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: The Elohim spoke to Noah, saying,
i18n.he: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־נֹ֥חַ לֵאמֹֽר׃
i18n.de: Da sprachen die Elohim zu Noah und sagten:
i18n.es: Los Elohim hablaron a Noé, diciendo:
i18n.fr: Les Elohim parlèrent à Noé, en disant :
i18n.ja: エロヒムはノアに語って言われた、
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 노아에게 말씀하시며 이르셨다,
i18n.ru: И говорили Элохим Ною, сказав:
i18n.zh: 厄罗音对挪亚说：
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音對挪亞說：

paragraphs.text: צֵ֖א מִן־הַתֵּבָ֑ה אַתָּ֕ה וְאִשְׁתְּךָ֛ וּבָנֶ֥יךָ וּנְשֵֽׁי־בָנֶ֖יךָ אִתָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: "Come out of the ark — you, your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives with you.
i18n.he: צֵ֖א מִן־הַתֵּבָ֑ה אַתָּ֕ה וְאִשְׁתְּךָ֛ וּבָנֶ֥יךָ וּנְשֵֽׁי־בָנֶ֖יךָ אִתָּֽךְ׃
i18n.de: "Geh aus der Arche — du, deine Frau, deine Söhne und die Frauen deiner Söhne mit dir.
i18n.es: «Sal del arca—tú, tu mujer, tus hijos y las mujeres de tus hijos contigo.
i18n.fr: « Sors de l'arche — toi, ta femme, tes fils et les femmes de tes fils avec toi.
i18n.ja: 「箱舟から出よ——お前と、お前の妻、お前の息子たち、お前と共にいる息子たちの妻たちと。
i18n.ko: "방주에서 나오라 — 너, 너의 아내, 너의 아들들, 너와 함께한 너의 며느리들도.
i18n.ru: «Выйди из ковчега — ты, и жена твоя, и сыновья твои, и жёны сыновей твоих с тобою.
i18n.zh: 「你要从方舟里出来——你和你的妻子、你的众子、你儿子们的妻子都要和你一同出来。
i18n.zh-Hant: 「你要從方舟出來—你、你的妻子、你的兒子們，以及你兒子們的妻子們，都同你出來。

paragraphs.text: כָּל־הַחַיָּ֨ה אֲשֶֽׁר־אִתְּךָ֜ מִכָּל־בָּשָׂ֗ר בָּע֧וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּבְכָל־הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ הוצא [הַיְצֵ֣א] אִתָּ֑ךְ וְשָֽׁרְצ֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָר֥וּ וְרָב֖וּ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Bring out with you every living thing that is with you, of all flesh — birds, cattle, every creeping thing that creeps upon the land — that they may swarm on the land, and be fruitful and multiply on the land."
i18n.he: כָּל־הַחַיָּ֨ה אֲשֶֽׁר־אִתְּךָ֜ מִכָּל־בָּשָׂ֗ר בָּע֧וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּבְכָל־הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ הוצא [הַיְצֵ֣א] אִתָּ֑ךְ וְשָֽׁרְצ֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָר֥וּ וְרָב֖וּ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Bringe mit dir alles Lebendige hinaus, das bei dir ist, von allem Fleisch — Vögel, Vieh, jedes Kriechtier, das auf dem Land kriecht — daß sie auf dem Land wimmeln und fruchtbar seien und sich mehren auf dem Land."
i18n.es: Saca contigo todo ser viviente que está contigo, de toda carne—aves, ganado, todo reptil que se arrastra sobre la tierra—para que pululen sobre la tierra, y sean fecundos y se multipliquen sobre la tierra».
i18n.fr: Fais sortir avec toi tout être vivant qui est avec toi, de toute chair — oiseaux, bétail, tout reptile qui rampe sur la terre — afin qu'ils foisonnent sur la terre, qu'ils soient féconds et se multiplient sur la terre. »

paragraphs.commentary: **The creation blessing repeated.** *Sharetzu ... peru u-rvu* — *swarm ... be fruitful and multiply* — is the explicit verbal echo of the creation blessings of Gen 1:22 (to the sea-creatures: 'be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters') and 1:28 (to humans: 'be fruitful and multiply, and fill the land'). paragraphs.commentary:
**Two firsts in one verse.** First *mizbeach* (altar) and first *olah* (whole burnt offering) in the Hebrew Bible. Cain and Hevel's earlier offerings (4:3–4) were *minchot* — gifts/grain-offerings — and were brought without a recorded altar. Here in 8:20 the cultic vocabulary that will run through Leviticus and Numbers makes its founding appearance: built altar, slaughtered offering, ascending smoke. The chapter places the institution of formal altar-and-burnt-offering at the post-Flood threshold — *before* circumcision (chapter 17), *before* the priesthood (Exodus 28), *before* the tabernacle (Exodus 25), but the cultic vocabulary they will all use is here.

The surplus from the seven-pair instruction (7:2) is what makes the offering possible — Noah has *extras* of the clean animals beyond breeding pairs, available for sacrifice. The chapter's earlier numerical instruction was the practical-cultic preparation for this moment. The two textual moves bind: 7:2 made room for surplus; 8:20 uses it.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The chapter's keystone verse — three load-bearing claims.**

First, *vayyarach YHWH et reach hannichoach* — *YHWH smelled the soothing aroma*. The Hebrew is anthropopathic and concrete: YHWH *smells* the rising smoke. The ANE parallel is unmistakable. In the *Atrahasis* epic and *Gilgamesh* Tablet XI, after the flood, Utnapishtim builds an altar and offers sacrifice, and *the gods smell the sweet savor and gather around it like flies* — because they have been starved during the flood (no human sacrifices reached them while humanity was drowned). Genesis's grammar of the *smelling* is exactly that of the Mesopotamian parallel, but Genesis's theology of it is different: the gods of *Atrahasis* are *hungry*, the YHWH of Genesis is *moved-to-resolve*. The verb and image are shared with the broader ANE flood traditions; the consequence drawn from the smelling differs.

Second, *lo osif l-qallel od et ha-adamah ba-avur ha-adam* — *I will not again curse the ground because of the human*. The chapter delivers on the hope Lamech named in 5:29: *the ground which YHWH cursed* (a callback to 3:17, *arurah ha-adamah ba-avurecha*) is now *not-going-to-be-cursed-again*. Note the verb-shift: 3:17 used אָרַר arar (the formal curse-pronouncement verb); 8:21 uses קָלַל qalel (a lighter curse-verb). The commitment is to *not adding* curses, not to *removing* the formal arar of 3:17. The post-Flood condition is *the curse stays operative; no new curses will be added*.

Third, *ki yetzer lev ha-adam ra mi-neurav* — *for the inclination of the heart of the human is evil from his youth*. The same diagnosis given as the reason for the Flood (6:5: *every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all day long*) is now given as the reason for *not repeating the Flood*. The exact same observation has produced opposite divine decisions. The rabbinic tradition (Rashi) reads the inversion as theological breakthrough: pre-Flood, human evil was the reason to destroy; post-Flood, recognition that human evil is *constitutional* (*mi-neurav* — from youth, present from the outset, structural rather than acquired) makes destruction-as-policy futile. Destruction did not solve the problem of human evil, because the problem is *in the yetzer* — in the inclining-faculty itself. The chapter's theology of divine restraint: rather than respond to human evil with cyclic destruction, the divine commits to continuity and lets the evil-prone humans persist. The Flood was the response that did not work; non-destruction is the response that follows.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Four pairs name the restored order.** *Zera v'qatzir* (seed and harvest — agricultural cycle), *qor va-chom* (cold and heat — thermal cycle), *qayitz va-choref* (summer and winter — seasonal cycle), *yom va-laylah* (day and night — diurnal cycle). The chapter closes with eight words that re-establish what the Flood had threatened.

Note the verb לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ lo yishbotu — *they shall not cease*. The root is שָׁבַת shabat — the root behind *shabbat*, the cessation. The cycles will *not sabbath*. The chapter is using the cessation-vocabulary in the negative: the rhythms that organize life will not stop, will not rest, will not cease. The Sabbath cycle (Gen 2:2–3) is, in Hebrew theology, the cessation that gives shape to the others; here at the post-Flood threshold the *other* cycles are promised *non-cessation*. The Sabbath cessation continues to structure the week, but the larger seasonal, diurnal, and agricultural rhythms continue without interruption. The chapter closes on the most basic guarantee the Hebrew Bible offers: the world's rhythms are pinned in place against another collapse like the Flood.
